chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام about a man who gives one Hajj to five persons, such that one of them goes out in it. Do they have a reward?
He said: “Yes, each one of them has the reward of a pilgrim.”
He said: So I said: Which of them has the greatest reward?
So he said: “The one whom the heat and the cold afflicted. And if he is a ṣarūrah, that does not suffice for them, and the Hajj belongs to the one who performed Hajj.”

key_terms.أَجْرٌ: reward granted by Allah for the act
key_terms.الْبَرْدُ: cold endured during the journey and rites
key_terms.الْحَرُّ: heat endured during the journey and rites
key_terms.حَاجٍّ: a pilgrim; here, one who receives the reward of pilgrimage
key_terms.حَجَّةً: a Hajj performance or pilgrimage being assigned or funded
key_terms.صَرُورَةً: one who has not yet performed his obligatory first Hajj
key_terms.لَمْ يُجْزِ: it did not suffice or discharge the obligation

ai.seo_question: If one Hajj is funded for several people but only one person performs it, do all of them receive reward and does it count for them?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the reward and legal effect of financing a single Hajj involving multiple people while only one person actually performs the journey. It teaches that all may receive reward, but the greatest reward is for the one who physically endures the hardship, and if the performer is doing his first obligatory Hajj, it does not fulfill the obligation on behalf of the others.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3129 - It is narrated from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Awwal (as) about a man who finances the Hajj for five people, but only one of them actually performs it. Does everyone receive a reward?
Imam (as) said: "Yes, each one of them receives the reward of a pilgrim."
I then asked: "Which of them has the greatest reward?"

Imam (as) replied: "The one who endures the heat and the cold. If the person is performing Hajj for the first time (ṣarūr), this does not suffice on behalf of the others, and the Hajj belongs to the one who performs it."
